title: Inside 162 mouse brain regions, between-region rules from input wiring and cell-type mix predicted unit spike physiology, but only the input rule kept a robust unique effect (IBL)
abstract: Question: earlier work split wiring and cell-type control of mouse brain physiology only between regions, where region identity goes together with every structural map. We tested the split inside regions at 100 um scale. Data: 52,753 IBL Brain-Wide Map units in 162 regions (139 mice), 9 intrinsic spike features; the Knox 2019 voxel connectome gave the afferent input profile at each unit position, and Allen MERFISH (two brains) gave the local neuron-subclass mix. Results: regions held 11.6% of unit variance and insertion offsets inside regions 15.5%; offsets were reliable but nearly not shared by nearby insertions of other mice. The planned test, which learned rules from within-region data, failed: unique out-of-region R2 was about 0 (cell types -0.0006, input -0.0001), although both beat a rotation null (p 0.018, 0.009; 110 draws). An exploratory test applied the between-region rules to within-region structure differences. Observed deviations followed the predictions with slopes 0.54 (cell types, 95% CI 0.35-0.70; second brain 0.32) and 0.45 (input, 0.25-0.64); rotation nulls gave 0 (p 0.005). Slopes stayed positive for interior units and after a border-bleed control. In a joint model, the input slope (0.35) was robust to position, insertion and map-noise controls; the unique cell-type slope (0.26) was not. The wiring share was 0.19 between regions and 0.78 inside regions (difference 0.59, CI 0.09-0.94). Limitations: correlational; exploratory post hoc tests; atlas maps from other mice; unit localisation error; explained within-region variance is below 0.4%.

display.caption: Between-region rules applied inside regions. a: observed against predicted within-region deviations (5% bins of units x features, 95% CI) for the cell-type and input maps. b: slopes for all units, units more than 200 um from the region edge, and with the border-bleed term removed; grey: rotation null 95%; lines: slope expected if the full rule acts locally, with 100 or 200 um localisation error. c: joint per-feature slopes.

The wiring versus cell-type split at two scales. a: wiring share uI/(uI+uT) between regions (cross-validated unique R2 of region means) and inside regions (joint regression of within-region deviations), with region-bootstrap 95% CI. b: joint within-region slopes of the cell-type and input predictions under three controls and with the second MERFISH brain as instrument.

Where unit physiology varies. a: variance shares of 9 z-scored features. b: insertion offsets are reliable inside an insertion (odd/even units) but not shared by the nearest insertion in another mouse (raw r, which has a negative centring bias). c: excess cross-mouse offset correlation by centroid distance against a centroid-shuffle null.
